utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-69-T. The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I've not been informed about any procedural issues. I repeat what I said yesterday because our information is that the medical situation of Mr. Stanisic is similar to yesterday, so what I said yesterday is still valid for today. Mr. Farr, are you ready to continue your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Dragicevic, I would like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you'll speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, the solemn declaration that you gave yesterday. Mr. Farr will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Dragicevic.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: To start with I just want to clear up one thing from yesterday. When I asked you who you knew to be the commander of the JSO, you said that it was Milorad Lukovic. Just so we are clear, Milorad Lukovic was also known as Legija; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Are you aware that he was also known as Milorad Ulemek?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. Returning to your work history now, in paragraph 4 of your statement you said that Jovica Stanisic was very angry when he heard that you were fired from your position at the federal MUP. Why was he angry?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably because of the manner in which this has been dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And what do you mean by that? What was it about the manner in which it was dealt with that made him angry?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the simple explanation was provided of me failing to seek permission from my superior and denying me the right to appeal the decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In your view, was there any kind of tension or mistrust between the federal MUP and the Serbian DB at the time you were dismissed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say that there was any sort of tension, rather, I would say that the federal MUP was in total disarray.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You go on to say that Jovica Stanisic hired you two or three weeks later. You must have been grateful to him for giving you a job so soon after you had lost the previous one; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. When a person ends up in such a dead-end situation, any way out is accepted with gratitude.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And is that especially true in light of the fact that you were hired at a relatively high level as a special advisor to the chief of the service?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, would you expect the witness to say no, at a lower level I would have been more happy? I mean, don't ask for the obvious, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 7 of your statement you said: "Following the assassination of the prime minister Djindjic I was replaced and I got retired." What is the link between Djindjic's assassination and your replacement and retirement?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following prime minister Djindjic's assassination I continued in the job of the chief of administration Chef de Cabinet and member of the council for national security. Three or four days after the assassination, I was summoned by the then BIA director who told me that I would no longer be able to perform these duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did he indicate that there was any link between Djindjic's assassination and you being dismissed?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did not indicate that at all. The issue raised was whether I -- or rather, I asked him if I met the requirements for retirement and he answered in the affirmative and I could tell by the expression of his face that he was relieved.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So you asked on your own initiative whether you could retire four days after Djindjic was assassinated; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Why did you wish to retire precisely at that time?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The work of the service as a whole went against some of my positions and views [Realtime transcript read in error "dues"].

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I guess what I'm trying to get at is the temporal link. You asked to be retired four days after Djindjic was assassinated. Was it at the moment that Djindjic was assassinated that the work of the service went against some of your positions and views, I think you may have said although the transcript says "dues"?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said the work of the service, I meant the appointment of certain individuals to certain posts, these being individuals without the requisite experience and not up to the tasks they were supposed to perform.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Were those appointments related to the Djindjic assassination in some way?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So is it your evidence that it's simply a coincidence that you asked to be retired four days after the Djindjic assassination?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps not. I apologise, the BIA director told me after my replacement that there was one other post in the service that I could occupy and that was the education centre. I declined with all due respect for the individuals who occupy such posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, I still don't think I understand you. What -- are you saying there's no link between your request to be retired and the Djindjic assassination? Was the fact the that Djindjic was assassinated related to the fact that you asked to be retired four days later, and if so, what was the link?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the point of the question. I don't understand. There is no link.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: That was the point of the question, sir. Were any allegations made against you at the time of the Djindjic assassination?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several days later I learned from the media, more precisely it was news carried on TV and the press, that I had been arrested. The explanation given was that I betrayed official information to a criminal group call the Zemun Clan which had been charged with organising and assassinating Prime Minister Djindjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: But those allegations had nothing to do with your request for retirement, or with your replacement; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was after my retirement.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. And what is your response to those allegations?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I called the BIA director on the phone and told him I just heard on or the TV that I was arrested while I'm here sitting in my home. What am I supposed to do? The answer I received was, nobody is consulting us on any matter anymore. My response to that was, well, then I will not be consulting anyone on anything either. I replaced the receiver and I never had contact with anyone in the security service again.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And what is your response to the allegation that you betrayed official information to the Zemun Clan? Is that true or false?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only connection with the Zemun Clan was the fact that I resided in Zemun. I felt highly uncomfortable and unsettling about it but the hardest hit was my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to the take-over of the federal SUP building by the Serbian DB. First of all, is it correct that you were already a member of the Serbian DB by the time this take-over occurred?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 8 of your statement you say this of the take-over: "I'm not sure, but I think an agreement about it existed between the federal and republic minister." When you refer to the federal minister, are you talking about Pavle Bulatovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Why do you think that this take-over was done with the agreement of Pavle Bulatovic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's nothing for me to think about it. I heard that this was the way things were done.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Whom did you hear that from?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your colleagues in the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, my colleagues who stayed in the federal SUP and joined the republican.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Were those colleagues in the federal SUP or the republican SUP at the time of the take-over?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were members of the federal SUP. After the take-over, the joint -- the republican SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we please have P2993 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, this document contains the minutes of the session of the council for reconciliation of standpoints regarding state politics held on the 2nd of November, 1992, about two weeks after the take-over of the federal MUP building.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: If we can have the top of the second page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: As you can see this meeting was attend by Milan Panic, Slobodan Milosevic, Momir Bulatovic, and the man who you say agreed to the take-over of the federal MUP building, Pavle Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: If we could have the third page in both languages, I'd like to read you an account of what Minister Bulatovic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: [As read] "Further on during the session, federal minister of Internal Affairs informed the members of the council about the event that took place on 18 October this year. On the aforementioned day, officers of the republic Ministry of Internal Affairs forcefully occupied the building of the federal Ministry of Internal Affairs located in the street Kneza Milosa 90 to 92. Once they were inside the building, the officers prohibited the employees of the State Security Service of the Federal Ministry of Internal Affairs to enter their offices. Taking over the building, the officers also took over its communications system, system of crypt protection, all equipment and technical devices of the State Security Service, documentation, registries, and the carpool." Sir, do you agree with me that these statements by Pavle Bulatovic clearly demonstrate that the take-over was by force and didn't take place as a result of an agreement between the federal and republican ministers?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've seen the document and I stand by my earlier statement, that I had only heard that there had been an agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 9 of your statement you indicated that you were not present when the take-over by the service came about. Where were you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I was not there. I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Are you aware that on the 27th of June, 1992, the police brigade of the federal MUP sent 17 of its members and brigade deputy commander Milorad Davidovic to the Republika Srpska with the aim of stabilising the security situation, establishing the legality of work and normal functioning of Internal Affairs organs, and ensuring the legitimacy of the organs of authority?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And I take it it follows then you are not aware of the resulting report in August 1992 in which Davidovic described the criminal activities of paramilitary groups in Bosnia, including Captain Dragan's Red Berets and a group belonging to Zivojin Ivanovic, aka Crnogorac, who according to the report was associated with the Serbian DB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know either.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You say of Captain Dragan in paragraph 79 of your statement: "I met him for the first time after the 5th of October 2000, when major rallies took place and there was a change of the regime in Serbia." Can you tell us as precisely as possible when you met Captain Dragan for the first time and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met Captain Dragan by coincidence in Belgrade several days after the events of the 5th of October. He was in the company of a man I knew. That was when we made our acquaintance.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And is it correct that that was a memorable experience given Captain Dragan's fame and notoriety?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw images of him on TV and of course I recognised him right away.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 79 of your statement you say: "I did not know of Captain Dragan in 1991. I heard of him afterwards but I did not know him." Then of course you continue to say that you met him after the 5th of October, 2000. My question is, when did you first hear of him?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't state a specific date, but his photographs were published widely in the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Would it have been in 1991 or 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you ever learn of any link or relationship between Captain Dragan and the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you ever learn about any links or relationship between Captain Dragan and Jovica Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: As far as you know, did Jovica Stanisic and Captain Dragan ever meet?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. For example, I never saw Captain Dragan in our building, and that was the only place where I was together with Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to your responsibilities as a member of the Serbian DB. In paragraph 12 of your statement you indicate that you became the head of the administration for internal co-operation within the Serbian DB in October 1992. In paragraph 10 you indicate that you received a decision appointing you to the position of special advisor to the chief of service. And in paragraph 12 you stated: "I submitted reports to my superior and exclusively to him. That is, to Jovica Stanisic." Was it normal for special advisors to the chief of service to report only to the chief?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The dates of my appointments are correct, so I simultaneously discharged two duties, the special advisor and the chief of administration. Now, in view of the nature of the business that I was in, I exclusively reported to the head of the service, i.e., Jovica Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you know whether other people who had the same title, that is special advisor to the chief, also reported only to the head of the service?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. There was a rule in the service which stipulated that everyone should stick to their scope of responsibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Because you reported only to Mr. Stanisic, the information you gave him would be available only to him and to anyone he chose to share it with; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I submitted my reports directly to Mr. Stanisic and it was up to him to decide which pieces of information or which reports would be forwarded up to the political leadership.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And because of the fundamental principle of secrecy that the DB operated under, he would have only shared that information with people who needed to know for the purposes of their work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think that's an objection -- sorry, this is an objection, but that's an invitation to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness has been asked quite a few things, I think, for which there's not been a very clear foundation. He certainly could know what Mr. Stanisic did with the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, is it correct that the DB operated under a fundamental principle of secrecy that dictated that information should only be shared with those people who needed the information for purposes of their work; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you know whether Jovica Stanisic followed that principle in his work?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not privy to where this information was forwarded, so I can only assume that he abided by those principles.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 76 of your statement you say: [As read] "I have never talked with Stanisic about the special operations unit, JSO, or any other unit. In fact, I did not talk about anything else but the above-mentioned topics regarding international co-operation." Doesn't that show that Stanisic operated on this need-to-know basis in his communication with you?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he was the head of the service. I was just a clerk doing a specific job. It was not my place to inquire with the chief of the service about what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And as a result of that, it's likely that you are unaware of the great majority of the things that Mr. Stanisic was doing and the great majority of the things that he knew during the time you worked with him; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can say is that Mr. Stanisic was fully informed about what I was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the question was a different one, not whether Mr. Stanisic was informed, but whether you had any knowledge of any matter outside the scope of your responsibilities that Mr. Stanisic dealt with.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] .... yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was a rule in our service stipulating that representatives of the service or members of the staff of the service are to do the specific jobs they were tasked with. I was in charge of international co-operation and I communicated with Mr. Stanisic exclusively on those issues. This is my answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And then Mr. Farr invites you on the following -- to give your answer to the following question: Would this mean that whatever Mr. Stanisic knew or did which was not within the scope of your assignment, that you would not be aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, turning now to your co-operation with foreign intelligence services while you were at the Serbian DB, in paragraph 15 of your statement you indicate that while Jovica Stanisic was the chief of the service, you maintained contacts with about 60 foreign services. The goal of these contacts and of this co-operation was to improve the intelligence position of both Serbia and the foreign countries with whom this co-operation was undertaken; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And the ultimate goal of that from the point of view of the Serbian service was to create a stronger, more stable, and more secure position for Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: With respect to the CIA in particular, in paragraphs 19 and 20 of your statement you indicate that you arranged the first secret meeting between Jovica Stanisic and person Number 1 in early 1992 when you were still in the federal service. Technically, according to the rules, you shouldn't have been arranging a meeting between a member of a foreign service and a member of a republican service at that time; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And similarly technically, Mr. Stanisic as a member of a republican service shouldn't have been meeting with a member of a foreign service; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was his personal decision, whether he wanted to do that or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: But it was contrary to the rules then in force; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of what the republican service rules were. I know, however, what the federal rules were.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: But the reality at that time was that Mr. Stanisic was the man with the information and authority necessary to be useful to the CIA; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And this meeting also indicates that the Serbian DB was already taking over the federal DB's function with respect to contacts with foreign services; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was an initial contact and it cannot be considered as taking over the whole function.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: But the beginning of that process?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one might say so.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 26 of your statement, you indicate that Stanisic was the only official in Serbia with whom the CIA could talk, and you go on to state that person Number 1: [As read] "... said to me that they, Americans, did not believe anyone other than Stanisic. By that I understood that they had trusted the State Security Service of Serbia too." The CIA obviously viewed Stanisic as a well-informed person capable of supplying accurate information regarding matters of interest to the CIA; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'd now like to turn to the UN hostage crisis. At paragraph 42 of your statement you say: [As read] "With finalisation of the hostage rescue mission, the crisis also ended and conditions were created for resumption of the peace talks with the Contact Group plan." How did the release of the hostages create the conditions necessary for resumption of the peace talks with the Contact Group plan?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because that was one of the preconditions for the resumption of the negotiations and the implementations of the Contact Group, i.e., to release the hostages and proceed with the implementation of the Contact Group agreement and to allow free movement of international forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So when you describe it as a precondition, is it your evidence that the Contact Group plan negotiations could not have resumed if the hostages had not been released?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only was it impossible for them to continue, but some more horrendous consequences would ensue such as air-strikes and the like.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the peace negotiations were taking on a particular urgency at this point in time from the perspective of the RS because the military situation of the RS and the VRS was becoming somewhat more difficult?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Was it also fair to say that Operation Flash in Croatia in May 1995 had weakened the strategic position of the RS and the VRS, the NATO bombing had weakened it further, and there was at least a possibility of more offensives from a strengthened Croatian army and Army of BiH?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to comment on that because I don't have the pertaining information.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Before we get into the actual events of the hostage crisis, in paragraph 35 you indicate that the leadership of the Republika Srpska MUP was involved in the proposal for mediation of the crisis. When you say the leadership of the Republika Srpska MUP, are you referring to Minister Rakic and Deputy Minister Kovac?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, Kovac was the deputy and I believe I saw an order signed by him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the Serbian DB had good co-operation with the Republika Srpska MUP at the time of the hostage crisis?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They gave them substantial assistance because they realised what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In paragraph 37 you say: [As read] "The negotiating mission of the service was approved by the minister and thus the government of Serbia as well as by the President of Serbia, Milosevic." When you say "minister" you are referring to Minister of the Interior Sokolovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, can I seek clarification of the answers. You said they gave them substantial assistance because they realised what it was all about. Do I understand that with "they" you referred to the Republika Srpska MUP and that "them" refers to the Serbian DB? Is that how I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Members of the MUP of Republika Srpska rendered enormous assistance because they realised that was the only way to get out of the crisis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the answer to my question is yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In your statement you describe the taking of the hostages and then in paragraph 35 you say: "At the same time the international community requested Serbia to influence that the hostages be freed." In paragraph 36 you say: "We were all aware that capturing UN hostages brought an enormous damage to FRY and Serbia." Is it fair to say that the release of the hostages was of great importance to the international community but also to Serbia's interest?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And by facilitating the release of the hostages, Serbia could undo some of the "enormous damage" to its interest that you referred to in paragraph 36; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You could even ask yourself whether it's not obvious from the statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And just so it's clear, that was at least one of the reasons for the negotiating mission; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And obvious. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, we agree that Jovica Stanisic went on this mission as a representative of President Milosevic, that he was accepted by the RS delegation as a representative of President Milosevic, that he described himself and was described by journalists as a representative of President Milosevic, and when the hostages were released he described that as "a big success of the president of the Republic of Serbia, Mr. Slobodan Milosevic." That's all correct as far as you know, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'd now like to play a short video-clip but before I do, can I ask you whether you recall acting as an interpreter for Mr. Stanisic at a press conference with Karadzic and Aleksa Buha shortly after the release of the hostages?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I tried to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is that the same we saw yesterday, Mr. Farr, where the witness testified that he worked as an interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a different occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd now like to play a short video-clip from the video with ERN V000-3182. The clip has 65 ter number 6309. And it runs from 11 minutes and 28 seconds to 12 minutes and 9 seconds. The transcripts have been provided to the booths marked as clip 1 and I will ask Mr. Laugel to begin playing and pause at 11 minutes and 53 seconds of the original which may be 25 seconds of this clip.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The transcript is bilingual which is actually a question, and then the same question translated into English; do we need to read it?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In this clip, the speech is all in B/C/S so, yes, the translators will need to read the translation for this one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Remaining UNPROFOR members, whom the army of Republika Srpska took prisoner after the bombing of Serbian civilian targets by NATO aviation, have been released today at 11.00. This was said at the press conference which was held by the President of Republika Srpska, Radovan Karadzic, Deputy President Nikola Koljevic, Minister of Foreign Affairs Buha and special envoy of president of Serbia, Jovica Stanisic in Pale this morning."

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, we've just heard a journalist refer to Mr. Stanisic as a special envoy of Mr. Milosevic which confirmed what you just said. What I want to ask you is that you on the far left-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is I, sitting to next to Aleksandar Buha, the foreign minister of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And I think we can agree that the man standing in the middle in the back of the room is Franko Simatovic and that he is wearing a camouflage uniform and a red beret; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And obviously you saw Mr. Simatovic dressed like this during your time on this mission?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, your statement contains three paragraphs on Mr. Simatovic. It talks about his position in the 2nd Administration. It talks about his relationship with Stanisic. It mentions his presence at hostage release negotiations. It says that he liked computers. It doesn't mention anything about him wearing a camouflage uniform and a red beret during your mission to Bosnia. Why is that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the first time that I see him in a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You mean this time in the courtroom, now is the first time you see him in a uniform? When you see this video?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: At this press conference was the first time you saw him in the uniform?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't consider that to be relevant. Why should I?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You didn't think it was relevant in the context of this case that Mr. Simatovic was wearing a camouflage uniform and red beret when he accompanied you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, is the witness assumed to be informed about this case or did he give his statement being questioned by a party? I mean, there's a suggestion in your question relevance for the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which requires --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I take your point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In the context of all of the matters that are addressed in your statement it didn't seem relevant to you there Mr. Simatovic was wearing a camouflage uniform and a red beret at this press conference?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was focused on so many things that I actually didn't pay attention to that detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Isn't it highly unusual that a person occupying the position of special advisor to the chief of the DB would be wearing a military uniform and a beret?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to reiterate that I was not interested in that. I didn't know anything about that because my remit and my terms of reference were completely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yesterday when I asked you whether you had any information that led you to believe that Franko Simatovic was a member of the DB special unit, you said no. Do you agree with me that being in the same room with Mr. Simatovic while he was dressed like this is information that could lead you to believe that Mr. Simatovic was a member of the DB special unit?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say again that I was so busy I didn't have time to think about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that Mr. Simatovic is fairly prominent in this group of men, all of whom are wearing suits, standing in the centre of the back of the room behind Radovan Karadzic in a camouflage uniform with a red beret?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I can answer the question, Mr. Farr, just by looking at the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I also asked you whether you had ever talked with Mr. Simatovic about the JSO or any other special DB unit and you said no. Are you really telling us that you never asked Mr. Simatovic, or Mr. Stanisic for that matter, why Mr. Simatovic was dressed this way?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. I'll ask Mr. Laugel to continue playing to the end of this clip.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Today we did important work. We achieved something very important with the special envoy of the President of Serbia Milosevic, Jovica Stanisic. I would like to give him the floor."

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I tender this clip as a Prosecution exhibit. It's 65 ter 6309.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be ...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number for 65 ter 6309 would be P3043, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'd now like to play a second clip from the same press conference. This begins immediately after the previous clip but this clip in fact has consecutive interpretation, I believe, done by the witness. So I would suggest that we simply play the clip as it is without having the booths read anything.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then we have nothing on the record, isn't it.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Well, the transcripts will be in evidence if it's admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The transcript will be in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes. This clip is from the video V000-3182 like the last one and it runs from 12 minutes and 8 seconds to 15 minutes and 22 seconds and I would ask Mr. Laugel to just play it straight through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I have perhaps one additional request, if the interpretation by the witness in this video-clip raises any concerns about the accuracy, I would like to hear comment from our interpreters because I'm totally unable to check what is translated, whether that's accurate or not. I know that this is a bit beyond what you are usually doing, but therefore I'm seeking your consent to assist the Chamber in this way, or otherwise, I would have to ask you to translate what is said in the original language which may make it even more confusing. Any problems with this proposition?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We'll do our best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm not asking the interpreters for a full review of the translation but whether there are any major mistakes. I notice that I'm more familiar with the word "release" rather than "releasement," but any specific comments?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is just that the speaker said mediating mission or mission as an intermediary which was left out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your comment. Mr. Farr, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, we just heard Mr. Stanisic -- we just heard Mr. Stanisic refer to "the former Bosnia and Herzegovina." This use of the word "former" to describe Bosnia and Herzegovina was common among Serb leaders at the time; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And is it fair to say that it expressed a belief that Bosnia and Herzegovina had ceased to exist as a republican state and that it would inevitably be replaced by two or more entities, one of which would be the Republika Srpska; is that a fair summary of how that term was used?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not put it that way, rather, I would say that at the time the term "former" was used to refer to all the republics of the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So it's your evidence that one would have heard references to the former Serbia at that time or the former Croatia or the former Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't either in Slovenia or in Croatia to speak of the former Serbia. I was in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's not an answer to the question. The question is, Mr. Farr is exploring your earlier answer that referring to the republics of the former Yugoslavia that you would refer to them as the former and then the name of the republic. Mr. Farr asked you whether you are aware of the same language being used for Croatia, the former Croatia or the former Serbia. Whether you were there or not has got nothing to do with the use of language in this context. Could you please answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that term was in use, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean the term, the former Croatia, or the former Serbia? Or the former Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, although by that point there was the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and since Serbia and Montenegro were still together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, reference was made not only to Serbia and to the federal republic but also to Croatia, and was Croatia ever referred to as the former Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably it was. I can't be positive at this time though.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was the phrase "the former Bosnia and Herzegovina" in any way related to the fact that Republika Srpska did not consider itself to be an integral part of a Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I would regard it more as a linguistic explanation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Towards the end of the clip, Mr. Stanisic says: "And that of course with a wish that Yugoslavia stays with the Serbian people in the Republic of Srpska." Mr. Stanisic was essentially saying that the FRY and Serbia would continue to stand behind and support the Republika Srpska, was that your understanding of his meaning?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding of the meaning of this sentence is that it expressed support for the Serbian people as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this clip as a Prosecution exhibit as well. It's 65 ter 6310.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear of no objections, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 6310 will receive number P3044, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the transcript is in what languages?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: The transcript attached is, in fact, just a verbatim transcript of exactly what we heard with B/C/S followed by English as interpreted by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So both the original language spoken and the interpretation as spoken in that video-clip?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P3044 is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, in addition to Franko Simatovic were there any other individuals with you on this mission dressed in camouflage uniforms and wearing red berets?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. The driver who was with me was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic would like to be excused but I note the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps it's time for a break anyhow. We'll take a break and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 11.00

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber apologises for the late start. We had to deal with some urgent matters. Mr. Farr, are you ready to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, just before the break I asked you whether you remembered any individuals other than Franko Simatovic wearing camouflage uniforms and red berets. You said you couldn't remember but the driver with you was in civilian clothes. Are you referring to the driver who drove you to the meeting in Pale that the Greek ministers attended, or is that another driver?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a different driver. When we went to Pale where the Greek foreign and defence ministers were present, I was driven by a driver who was in camouflage uniform and you have footage to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Right. And I think we agree he was in camouflage uniform with a red beret and had an automatic rifle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And there were three or four other similarly dressed men with you when you arrived at that meeting, not necessarily in your vehicle, but accompanying you, is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: But you didn't understand this group of three or four men wearing red berets and camouflage uniforms to be a unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understood them to be a security detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to turn now to the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr, security provided by whom or by what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The security provided by the State Security Service of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'm just going to play a short clip. This is from P2977. The clip is from 30 minutes to 31 minutes of that video which is V000-7024 but I am going to ask actually that we just play through 30 minutes and 30 seconds, please. And sorry, can I say this should be played without sound, there may be subtitles, but we are not relying on them, we just want the witness to look at the picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, the images we've just seen show your arrival at the meeting in Pale that the Greek ministers attended; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And can we now play from this point to 31 minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, are you able to say whether the rest of the footage that we just saw from 30 minutes and 30 seconds to 31 minutes was also from the time of the hostage crisis?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The beginning of the film shows us leaving Pale. Mr. Simatovic and I were seated in the back of the jeep.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: What about the footage of Mr. Stanisic getting in a helicopter, was that from the time of the hostage negotiations, are you able to say?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to turn now to the negotiations surrounding the release of the hostages. You indicated in your statement that Mr. Simatovic was present during the negotiations with the VRS leadership in Han Pijesak but you didn't say whether he was present during the negotiations with the political leaders in Bijeljina. Do you recall whether Mr. Simatovic was present for those negotiations as well?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly if Mr. Simatovic was present in Bijeljina. I do know, however, that he accompanied Mr. Stanisic and me to see General Mladic in Han Pijesak and that from there we went on to Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You indicated that Babic and Martic were both present in Bijeljina when you went to meet Karadzic and Krajisnik. Do you agree that this shows there was close co-operation between the political leaders of the RS and the RSK?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You also indicated that they were discussing the possibility of uniting the RS and RSK at the time. Is it correct that this was part of an ultimate goal or plan that all Serbs live in one state?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your conclusion is too comprehensive, all Serbs in one state. I would limit this to the point when a decision was taken that Republika Srpska should unite with the Republic of the Serbian Krajina. At that point the relations between the leadership of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the political leaderships of the Republic of Serbian Krajina and Republika Srpska were quite troubled. The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia had introduced sanctions. As we arrived in Bijeljina, as you, yourself, said and I stated myself, we found Mr. Babic and Martic there from the Republic of the Serbian Krajina, as well as Mr. Krajisnik and Karadzic from Republika Srpska. Mr. Stanisic -- may I continue? Or?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I think you've answered my question at this point unless the Chamber requires more information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'd like to turn now to the negotiations with Karadzic. Mr. Jordash played you a video of an interview with Mr. Karadzic yesterday in which Mr. Karadzic said -- well, he was asked how the Serbian leadership managed to persuade him to release the hostages and his answer in part was: "... by suggestions and incentives and that's why we have accepted the suggestions of President Milosevic." Now, it seems to me in your testimony yesterday you talked about suggestions that Mr. Stanisic gave but you didn't mention anything about incentives he provided, and I want to explore that. At page 39 and 40 of yesterday's transcript, you indicated that Mr. Karadzic asked for logistical support from Serbia but that you couldn't promise anything but you also said that you couldn't say what kind of logistical support he was asking for because you were not present during all of the conversations. So, in fact, as far as you know, it's entirely possible that Mr. Karadzic requested military support from Jovica Stanisic in the form of Special Police Units or paramilitary units. You can't exclude that possibility, can you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Well, I think it's a slightly unfair or if not unfair then unhelpful question. I mean, the witness can't exclude anything if he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. And it's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I suppose -- as I understood the witness's evidence, he was purporting to tell us everything, as I understood it, that were the reasons that Mr. Stanisic used to persuade the Bosnian Serb leadership. If we agree that there may have been incentives that this witness doesn't know about, then I'm happy with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- is that something we would have to explore, either the witness knows anything about incentives or he doesn't know anything about incentives. Now, if he doesn't know about incentives, then how would he be in a position to exclude, until, of course, he would have very specific confirmation of there never having been any incentives. Now, usually if - but this is common knowledge - if someone says five times that there were no incentives, some people start asking themselves whether there were any incentives. So, therefore, the witness says he doesn't know about it, therefore, I would say, logically, unless he has any specific reason to say not only that he has no knowledge about it, but that he has knowledge that there were no incentives, and then of course he should be invited to tell us on what this knowledge that there were no incentives is based. If such a thing doesn't come up, then of course the witness cannot exclude any possibility, as no one could. Mr. Farr, is this -- my analysis of the situation if that is understood and accepted both by Mr. Jordash and by you, Mr. Farr, then we can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the issue I was trying to get is exactly what you've raised. Does the witness have any specific reason -- specific knowledge. If he has no --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then you should not ask him whether he can exclude further possibility, but then you should ask the witness whether he has any specific knowledge which would give him a basis to conclude that there no incentives were used. That's then the question you would like to put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And Mr. Jordash you would have no problem with such a question?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: No, and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's see whether the witness -- Do you have any specific knowledge which would allow you to conclude that incentives did not play a role whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I truly have no knowledge of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: May I just clarify that that answer applies to both the political and the military leadership of the RS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the question was unspecific. That is, if you say if you have no specific information on the basis of which you can positively state that there were no incentives that would be both true for the military leaders and for the political leaders, is that -- I see you are nodding yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to rise to my feet. I hadn't appreciated that it's part of the Prosecution case that there were incentives and, as yet, the Prosecution haven't indicated what their case is on this issue, so I just put that on the record. I don't know whether the Prosecution allege military incentives.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe in our 98 bis submissions we did indicate that it's our case that there's a linkage between Mr. Stanisic's presence in Bosnia in this time in May and June of 1995 and events that relate to units that we say he is associated with at a later period.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the incentives, you then understand the incentives to be continuation of activities of a unit? I would not consider this to be an incentive, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Or if I may say so adequate notice at the Rule 98 stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's -- I suggest you have put it on the record, Mr. Jordash. Let's proceed. Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we please have P942 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to turn now to some of the reasons for the hostages release. Sir, that is document entitled: "Decision regarding the strategic goals of the Serbian people in Bosnia and Herzegovina." It comes from the Official Gazette of the Serbian People in B&H, which indicates that the decision was made by the session of the Assembly of the Serbian people in B&H held on 12 May 1992. It lists six strategic goals including: "1. Border separation of the state from the other two national communities. 2. Corridor between Semberija and Krajina. 3. Creation of the corridor in the valley of Drina River, meaning elimination of the Drina River as the border between Serbian states." Did you ever hear of these six strategic goals?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the first time I've seen this document. Besides, I did live in the Republic of Serbia. I cannot possibly comment on something that is a decision of the leadership of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: My question was just whether you had ever heard of these either in a public speech by Mr. Krajisnik or Mr. Karadzic, through the media or in your personal contact with those men other otherwise, have you heard of the six strategic goals of the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, do you agree with me that the Contact Group plan offered the chance to consolidate and legalise gains made by the Serb side in the war in Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And is it, in fact, the reason that Milosevic and Stanisic wanted to have the hostages released was because the hostage-taking jeopardised this opportunity to consolidate and legalise these claims because it jeopardised the Contact Group talks; is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we please move into private session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Could I just inquire as to the page numbers that my learned friend wants to rely upon in 6303.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: It's Milosevic's speech on page 6 in English. Well, in any event, I believe it begins on page 6. We'd like to have the whole of the speech. Unfortunately in my notes, I don't have the last page but --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: That particular speech finishes on page 17. Is that ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: That's it, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 11 pages to read, Mr. Jordash. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, there's just one thing I neglected to asked you earlier when we were talking about co-operation with the CIA. I assume you agree with me that the fact that a person or a government co-operates with the CIA doesn't necessarily mean that that person or government has never committed any crimes?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you say so, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: All right. I'd now like to turn to the awards ceremony at Kula. In page 72 of your statement, you say that you were in charge of protocol which you define as who stood where and in what order the programme would go on. Did you have any responsibilities related to arranging awards for the people who received awards?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If I may say so, I was the supervisor of the protocol which means that I had already received paperwork prepared in advance and on that a basis I constructed the whole protocol.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So you received in advance the names of the people who were to receive awards and of the other people involved in the ceremony; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And you were actually present on the day of the ceremony, is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And, in fact, at one point in the proceedings, you called out the names of the people who were receiving awards, as they received their awards from Mr. Stanisic; is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I would now like to show a series of short clips from the Kula video but before I do one more question. In paragraph 84 of your statement, you say of Mr. Stanisic: "I know how he behaves and reacts. For instance, he never yelled if he was angry." Is it fair to say that he is a person who tends not to show much emotion whether positive or negative?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for this specific instance, I would say that I have to admit, I didn't include it in my statement. However, after I gave it quite a lot of thought, I think that he wasn't physically capable --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please rephrase his answer. The interpreters couldn't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you repeat your last answer because the interpreters had difficulties in hearing you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that apart from being angry about probably some other things relating to the protocol, I also think that he was suffering from some medical condition at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: I'm not asking about a specific instance. I'm asking in general, is he someone who didn't tend to show strong emotion, whether positive or negative?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Okay. We will now look at a series of clips from the Kula video which has been admitted as P61. The first clip begins at 53 seconds and ends at 1 minute and 20 seconds. The transcript has been marked as "Kula clip 1" for the booths and I will ask Mr. Laugel to just play that clip through.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "Veterans of the special operations unit of the Republic of Serbia State Security lined up for your inspection. Colonel Zika Ivanovic reporting. Stanisic: How are you? Good. Am I one of them? ZI: Certainly not one of the veterans. JS: /inaudible/ excuse me? Veterans /inaudible/."

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, were you present at that point?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was standing nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: We've just seen Mr. Stanisic shake hands with someone who introduced himself at Zika Ivanovic. Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was the first time that I saw him.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Is there any -- as a matter of protocol, is there any significance to the fact that he is the person who presented the other veterans? Did that indicate some specific status or importance?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that is -- was their decision to decide who would be the person to report.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: You didn't have any involvement in that in your facilitation of the protocol?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: He says that he will be presenting the veterans of the unit. Doesn't that imply that these men had combat experience and therefore that the unit existed before you say it started in 1996?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally think that what happened here was a kind of misunderstanding of the meaning of the word "veteran". I would prefer to refer to them as men who had specific skills and knowledge that were valuable in the course of the training of the unit as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we now play the next clip which begins at 9 minutes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can I ask some clarification in relation to that last answer. You rephrase more or less the qualification of veterans. Do you know any of those who were present at the time? Do you know any of the members of the unit or at least those who were present being presented as veterans?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to ask you to instruct me whether I'm allowed to name any names with regard to your question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If they are still at this moment active, then we'd have to move into private session. Perhaps out of an abundance of caution, we should -- perhaps you do not know. Or are they all former people who do not serve in the service anymore?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, they are not in the service anymore, the ones that I knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those are the men that I knew through support because we trained judo together, such as Mr. Rajo Bozovic, and later we socialised through football clubs. I also knew Zvezdan Jovanovic and Nikola Loncar. Zvezdan Jovanovic was that person opening the door to the jeep when I was alighting from the jeep at Pale. And as I said, Nikola Loncar as well. So these were the three that I was acquainted with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The people you are now describing are the ones who were dressed and in camouflage uniform with red berets? Or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. They were wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At this event in 1995?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mid-1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Farr, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, correct me if I'm wrong, but did you mention in your statement that you knew Rajo Bozovic and Nikola Loncar? I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did mention that in my statement. I think that I was asked about specific names. I cannot recall, however. Maybe we can look and check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you mentioned Mr. Bozovic. Did you know him from before this Kula ceremony? Or ...?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. We were both training judo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I read from -- I read from paragraph 78, also in relation to 77. 77 says: "At the time of the Kula ceremony the JSO was an anti-terrorist unit but I'm not sure how many members it had." Then you say that you saw Legija several times in Kula. "I met Rajo Bozovic for the first time in Kula. I had not known him beforehand."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw Rajo Bozovic for the first time in Kula. Maybe that's the error. Because I didn't know that he was a member of that unit. I used to know him from the period when he was a civilian. Perhaps that's what this error is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked you when you referred to Mr. Bozovic as one of the veterans, where you say they were not real veterans, I asked you did you know him from before this Kula ceremony. Then you said, yes, we were both training judo. Whereas it seems that from paragraph 77 and 78 you say that you didn't know him and you met him for the first time in Kula.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I say that it is possible that there was a misunderstanding. I understood that I was asked whether I saw him for the first time in uniform at that celebration and before that I had never been to Kula.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your answer was in the understanding of my question being whether you had seen Mr. Bozovic any earlier in uniform, that's how you understood my question, and then you said -- no, my question was simply did you know him before the Kula ceremony, and you said yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In paragraph 78, you say: "I met Rajo Bozovic for the first time in Kula." And that's not only what you said, but you said: "I had not known him beforehand." There's no reference whatsoever as to whether you knew him in uniform or without a uniform. There's nothing in there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I say, there might have been a misunderstanding. What I meant was that I had never seen him in a uniform and as a member of the unit. That's what I meant to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Farr.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, when you gave your -- when you gave your statement, one of the interviewers was a woman who you spoke with in Serbian. Of course you also speak English very well as we've heard. Can you explain how it's possible that your statement that you saw Rajo Bozovic in uniform for the first time in Kula made it into your statement as "I had not known him before then"?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think I already explained that in my exchange with the presiding judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we now play the next clip which begins at 9 minutes and 3 seconds and ends at 9 minutes and 43 seconds. The transcript has been marked as "Kula clip 2" for the booths.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "ZI: Mr. President, veterans of the special operations unit of the Republic of Serbia state security are lined up for inspection. Colonel Zika Ivanovic reporting. SM: Hello, Ivanovic. ZI: Mr. President, allow me to introduce the unit's veteran officers. Mr. President, Colonel Radojica Bozovic. Milosevic: Hello, Bozovic, I read those reports of yours. RB: Thank you. /inaudible/ God forbid there should be more of them, but should there be, I'm here."

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: We've just heard Milosevic say to Radojica Bozovic that he has read some of his reports. Did you ever read or see any of these reports of Bozovic that Milosevic refers to?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: And the fact that these -- that he was writing these reports is not something that ever came up in your conversations with him during your acquaintance?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As I already said, we didn't see each other that frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, the fact that Milosevic has read these reports shows that he is better informed about these people in this unit than you were; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Sorry to object, but it's an invitation to speculate. He is asking the witness to look into the minds not only of Bozovic but also Milosevic and not only look into their minds but conclude that they were thinking the reports were about a unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Your Honour, one of the premises of this witness's evidence, as I understood it, was that he was able to look into minds and know what people were thinking about and part of that involves a contention that he was -- that he was able to know what Mr. Stanisic was thinking by watching him while Frenki gave a speech. He is purporting to have knowledge that I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say if he can read the mind of others which is, of course, not what we expect the witness to tell us about first, I will respond to that by asking him similar questions and to read minds of even other persons. I think let's stick to the facts. From the words of Mr. Milosevic it seems that he had read the reports. Whereas this witness says I've not read the reports. That distinction may be clear. We've heard from this witness what he knew about the unit or may not have known about the unit, what the limits were of his knowledge and his activities, and to know whether Mr. Milosevic knew more, we would have to know what his knowledge was apart from this one specific point about having read the reports. Let's stick to the facts and move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, in this clip we've seen Zika Ivanovic, Radojica Bozovic and other men dressed in camouflage uniforms with red berets. Those were other uniforms that you saw Mr. Simatovic wearing during the hostage crises and that you saw other members of your DB security wearing during the hostage crisis; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we now please play the next clip which runs from 13 minutes and 35 seconds to 14 minutes and 10 seconds, and the transcript is marked "Kula clip 3" for the booths.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "One of its most recent successes was its engagement in the freeing of 400 UNPROFOR hostages in Republika Srpska, which was met with a very positive response by the international community and made our country's position stronger."

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, this is a clip from Mr. Simatovic's speech at the Kula awards ceremony. Were you actually present when Mr. Simatovic gave that speech?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, and you can see me in the video-clip.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: We've just heard Mr. Simatovic say that the unit participated in the release of the UNPROFOR hostages. You know that Zvezdan Jovanovic was present at the time of the release of the UNPROFOR hostages and you also know him to be a member of the unit in 1997 at the time of this ceremony; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: We also just heard Mr. Simatovic say that the release of the UNPROFOR hostages "met with a very positive response in the international community and made our country's position stronger." That confirms that the goal of the hostage release was to strengthen Serbia's position, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among other things, yes. The basic objective was to rescue the prisoners and to send them back to their units. I wouldn't put the position of Serbia in front of that or as something more important than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Do you agree that the other considerations you've mentioned were not mentioned in Mr. Simatovic's speech?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to what I just said?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: In other words, Mr. Simatovic indicated that the release of the hostages strengthened Serbia's position?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I only added to that what was my view. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Can we please play the next clip which runs from 15 minutes 21 seconds to 15 minutes 52 seconds. This clip we will play without sound but before we start --

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, this is a short clip in which the cameraman pans across the group assembled in the room. I'm going to ask you to look for yourself and note the time-code, that is the minutes and seconds at the bottom right-hand corner of the screen at the moment you appear. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: So let's start playing the clip and we'll play through.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Sir, did you see yourself in that clip?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARR
utterances.text: Did you note the time-code?

utterances.speaker: VLADO DRAGICEVIC [Resumed]
